jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Zambia's AI governance rests on the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2026 of the Ministry of Technology and Science, launched in November 2024, which promises a National AI Council, AI ethics guidelines, regulatory sandboxes and an AI mandate for the communications regulator ZICTA; none of these has yet been set up by any instrument. The Data Protection Act 2021 regulates automated decisions and profiling, and the Securities and Exchange Commission's 2020 sandbox guidelines name AI as a category of innovation that can be tested. In June 2025 the National Assembly passed a motion urging the Government to develop a policy and legal framework for AI, and a replacement data protection bill covering AI has been announced but not published.
lead_institutions: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
narrative.review_notes: On 18 October 2026 the AI strategy and the Data Protection Act 2021 were checked against their official texts on the technology ministry's and Parliament's websites, and Parliament's records, the ICT regulator, the central bank and the standards body were checked. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the data protection commissioner, Smart Zambia, the cyber security agency and the remaining sector regulators and ministries, which is still pending.

instruments.current_status: Zambia's first national AI strategy, covering 2024-2026, published by the Ministry of Technology and Science, which reported its launch in Lusaka on 21 November 2024. The cover gives the period 2024-2026 while the page headers of the same document read '2025 - 2027'. The strategy announces a National AI Council, sector Technical Working Groups, a National Emerging Technologies Centre of Excellence, AI ethics guidelines and regulatory and data sandboxes, and proposes extending ZICTA's mandate to AI regulation and ethical compliance; no implementing instrument for these was found.
instruments.summary: Zambia's first national AI strategy, issued by the Ministry of Technology and Science with a foreword by the Minister, sets a vision of Zambia as a destination for 'AI for Emerging Economies' and strategic pillars on policy and regulation, human capital and AI literacy, digital infrastructure and data, research and innovation, and sector adoption (health, agriculture, education, mining, climate, public services). For governance it proposes a National AI Council advising the ministry, sector Technical Working Groups, Smart Zambia coordinating AI adoption across government and a Centre of Excellence, and it calls for national AI ethics guidelines, regulatory and data sandboxes and extending the ZICTA regulator's mandate to AI regulation and ethical compliance. It includes a phased implementation plan and a monitoring and evaluation framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only national AI-specific policy document; anchors Zambia's planned AI governance structure and regulatory agenda.

instruments.current_status: Act No. 3 of 2021 of the National Assembly (date of assent 23 March 2021; dated 24 March 2021 in the Act). Under section 1 it comes into operation on a date appointed by the Minister by statutory instrument; the commencement order was not found on an official site (reported in other sources as 1 April 2021). Cabinet was reported (non-official sources, 24 April 2025) to have approved in principle a bill to repeal and replace the Act to cover AI, machine learning and data analytics; no such bill appears on the National Assembly's bills list (see leads).
instruments.summary: Zambia's general data protection law, establishing the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner, principles for processing personal data, registration of data controllers and processors, licensing of data auditors and data subject rights. Section 62 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal effects or similarly affects them (except where necessary for a contract, authorised by written law or based on explicit consent, with safeguards including human intervention and the right to contest the decision), and bars automated processing of sensitive personal data without express consent, public interest or a legal basis with safeguards. Section 58 entitles data subjects to information about the basic logic involved in automated decision making, and section 46 requires a data protection impact assessment where automated processing, including profiling, produces legal or similarly significant effects.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only binding Zambian law with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.
instruments.evidence_reference: local-retry-2026-10-18: National Assembly page https://www.parliament.gov.zm/node/8853 opened (HTTP 200, title 'The Data Protection Act, 2021') and its linked 40-page official PDF read via curl; title, Act number, date of assent (23rd March, 2021), date [24th March, 2021], s.1 commencement, s.46, s.58 and s.62 checked against the record. A copy is also listed on the Ministry of Technology and Science Downloads page.

instruments.official_title: Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines for Capital Markets (Guideline No. 3 of 2020)
instruments.english_title: Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines for Capital Markets (Guideline No. 3 of 2020)
instruments.current_status: Dated 9 December 2020; published on the SEC guidelines page (current PDF uploaded May 2026). It is a general fintech sandbox in which 'Artificial Intelligence' is one of the listed application categories and AI is named in the definition of 'innovation'; it has no AI-specific requirements. Gazette listings suggest a 2026 notice of the guidelines (Gazette of 8 May 2026), not reviewed.
instruments.summary: Securities and Exchange Commission guideline, issued under its Securities Act mandate, creating a regulatory sandbox in which capital-market innovations can be live-tested under conditions and limitations designed to protect investors, without full adherence to all regulatory obligations. It defines eligible innovations to include artificial intelligence and automated investment advice and lists 'Artificial Intelligence' among the admissible application categories, and sets eligibility criteria and five stages (application, preparation, testing, exit, commercial deployment) with revocation and oversight rules.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulatory sandbox that expressly admits AI-based capital-market innovations for supervised testing.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): SEC guideline page and 20-page PDF read (pdftotext); dated 9 December 2020 in the document.
